criteria.adapter_cancel: Callers get a dedicated cancel call that flags the handle, frees the native writer without finishing it so no key appears, turns later handle use into a state failure, and documents leftover server-side parts as the bucket policy's job.
criteria.delete_on_cancel: Cancellation removes the destination key outright, destroying any object a previous upload already placed there.
criteria.drop_only: Callers get no cancellation call and simply release the handle; the writer never finishes and no key appears, but nothing closes explicitly and reuse past abandonment has no declared failure.

cancel.instructions: What cancellation shape should multipart uploads offer?

criteria.custom_signer: Header control arrives through an adapter-written signer, reimplementing the signature scheme the runtime already provides.
criteria.emulate_via_type: The type knob doubles as a mandatory Content-Type, although measurements prove a conflicting Content-Type still uploads, so the guarantee would be hollow.
criteria.method_negatives: Only the negatives the platform enforces, wrong-method use and forged signatures failing closed, enter the contract; header requirements stay inexpressible and go on record as a platform gap.

signed_headers.instructions: Which standing should required presigned-URL headers take in the contract?

criteria.epoch_millis: Last-modified times travel as plain integer counts of milliseconds since the epoch.
criteria.iso_string: Last-modified times travel as ISO-8601 formatted strings.
criteria.opaque_instant: Last-modified times travel as opaque time::instant values built by time::instant_from_epoch_millis.

timestamps.instructions: Which Can value should carry object timestamps?

state: For B1-10, Can targets pinned Bun 1.4.2 (bun-1.4.2-darwin-arm64-v1, revision 744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99) and exposes S3 object storage through the native S3Client, with every behavior below measured live against MinIO. All adaptation stays in runtime/platform/s3.ts behind a single emitter binding, and the adapter may only drive native operations, never reimplement request signing. Measured presign behavior: the only knobs are expiresIn, method and type, so callers cannot bind required headers; issued URLs expose the X-Amz-Algorithm, X-Amz-Credential, X-Amz-Date, X-Amz-Expires, X-Amz-Signature and X-Amz-SignedHeaders parameters with no secret material; GET serves 200; a PUT-signed URL used with GET, or a GET-signed URL used with PUT, serves 403; corrupting X-Amz-Signature serves 403 and a corrupted PUT stores nothing; sending a typed PUT under another Content-Type still serves 200, proving the type is advisory; expiresIn of zero or less raises TypeError, as does any method besides GET, PUT, DELETE or HEAD; signed GET against a missing key serves 404; signed DELETE serves 204 and the object disappears; signed HEAD serves 200 with its length. Measured upload behavior: the writer is a NetworkSink with write, flush, end and close and no abort operation; partSize under 5242880 raises RangeError; end resolves to the byte total rather than an etag; post-end writes vanish silently while repeated end calls succeed; closing a writer without end leaves no key behind; ending an empty writer resolves 0 and stores a zero-byte object. Measured download behavior: slice windows return exact bytes except slice(n,n), which yields the one byte at n; cancelling a download reader finishes the stream. Stat exposes its fields non-enumerably; the etag keeps its quotes and multipart uploads add a -N suffix; lastModified arrives as a Date; stored text types acquire a charset suffix while Blob types on write are dropped. Measured listing behavior: maxKeys pages set isTruncated and hand back a nextContinuationToken that continues without overlap; a delimiter collects groups into commonPrefixes; each entry shows key, eTag, lastModified, size and storageClass; unknown prefixes return no entries. Measured failures: absent keys give exists false, size null, and unlink/delete true, but stat, text, bytes, json and stream raise S3Error NoSuchKey; bad credentials raise S3Error UnknownError; an absent bucket also reads as NoSuchKey; a refused endpoint raises S3Error ConnectionRefused. Timestamp conversion can reuse time::instant_from_epoch_millis and time::instant_epoch_millis from the catalogue.
